# ButtonGroup

Figma: [02e. ButtonGroup](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-893) · Family: 02 Actions · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-05-20

A layout container for grouping multiple Button instances together. Controls orientation, spacing, alignment, and direction. Used for form footers, dialog actions, and any UI surface where related actions sit together.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/button-group/reference.png`

### ButtonGroup

A chromeless layout container that places two or three Button instances with consistent orientation, spacing, alignment and reading-order direction.

Level: organism · Contains: Button

Use when:
- Dialog and BottomSheet footers with Confirm plus Cancel
- Card-level CTAs on a deal card (Invest plus Details)
- Onboarding Skip plus Continue: Alignment=space-between
- Narrow mobile sheets where actions must stack: Orientation=vertical

Don't use when:
- There is only one action: use a single Button
- Four or more actions: keep one primary Button and move the rest into a Menu
- Buttons that share edges to switch a view or a value: use SegmentedControl_2 (or _3/_4/_5)
- Selectable filter chips: use Tag Group

Accessibility: Button 1 is the primary in reading order, so the visual flip in Arabic keeps the same screen-reader order; switch to vertical rather than truncating labels.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

ButtonGroup is a layout container - it has no visual chrome of its own. Its job is to position 2 or 3 Button instances together with consistent spacing, alignment, and direction. Use it anywhere multiple related actions sit side-by-side.

On Safqah surfaces, ButtonGroup is most often used in dialog footers (Confirm/Cancel), form actions (Save/Cancel/Reset), card-level CTAs on deal cards (Invest/Details), and bottom-sheet primary actions.

### At a glance

| Dialog footer · end-aligned | Form action bar · space-between | Vertical stack · centered |
| --- | --- | --- |

### Anatomy

ButtonGroup is a thin layout shell. It exposes three button slots and four axes that control how those slots arrange themselves.

| Button 1 Primary action (semantically first). In LTR horizontal, leftmost. In RTL horizontal, visually rightmost. | Button 2 Secondary or alternative action. Pair with Button 1 in dialog footers and form actions. | Button 3 Optional tertiary action. Hidden by default. Enable via "Show Button 3" boolean - use sparingly. | Container No visible chrome - invisible layout frame. All visual weight comes from the buttons themselves. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

### Orientation

ButtonGroup supports two orientations. Choose based on available width and the relationship between actions.

horizontal

Default. Buttons sit side-by-side. Use for dialog footers, form actions, card-level CTAs. Most common.

vertical

Buttons stack. Use when width is constrained (narrow mobile, bottom sheets) or when actions need equal visual weight.

### Spacing

Three spacing options control the gap between buttons. All map to semantic Spacing variables.

tight

Spacing/8 (8 dp)

Use for closely-paired actions where the actions feel like a unit.

default

Spacing/12 (12 dp)

Material 3 spec. The right choice for most dialog footers and form action bars.

loose

Spacing/16 (16 dp)

Use when buttons need visual separation - when actions have different importance.

### Alignment

Alignment controls how buttons sit along the primary axis of the group. The right choice depends on conventions and content priority.

start

Buttons hug the leading edge. Use when the group sits inline with body content.

center

Buttons sit in the middle of the container. Use in confirmation modals, success states.

end

Buttons hug the trailing edge. The conventional choice for dialog footers (primary on the right in LTR).

space-between

Buttons spread to opposite edges. Use for asymmetric pairs like "Skip" / "Continue" in onboarding.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

ButtonGroup inherits a Direction axis from the broader Safqah system. In RTL contexts, the horizontal layout reverses - Button 1 (primary) sits on the visual right, Button 2 (secondary) to its left.

LTR

Default. Primary action sits on the right of the row (Material 3 and web conventions).

RTL

Arabic context. Primary action sits on the left of the row. Auto-layout flip handles this - no separate template needed.

### Code examples

ButtonGroup is a thin layout shell - it maps directly to a Row/Column with controlled spacing in code.

### Flutter

```dart
// Horizontal · end-aligned · default spacing (dialog footer)
SafqahButtonGroup(
  orientation: ButtonGroupOrientation.horizontal,
  spacing: ButtonGroupSpacing.default_,
  alignment: ButtonGroupAlignment.end,
  children: [
    SafqahButton(
      variant: SafqahButtonVariant.tertiary,
      label: 'Cancel',
      onPressed: () => Navigator.pop(context),
    ),
    SafqahButton(
      variant: SafqahButtonVariant.primary,
      label: 'Confirm',
      onPressed: _onConfirm,
    ),
  ],
)

// Vertical · centered (narrow mobile, equal-weight actions)
SafqahButtonGroup(
  orientation: ButtonGroupOrientation.vertical,
  spacing: ButtonGroupSpacing.default_,
  alignment: ButtonGroupAlignment.center,
  children: [
    SafqahButton(variant: SafqahButtonVariant.primary, label: 'Browse deals', onPressed: _browse),
    SafqahButton(variant: SafqahButtonVariant.secondary, label: 'Open portfolio', onPressed: _portfolio),
  ],
)
```

### React (token-driven)

```dart
<SafqahButtonGroup orientation="horizontal" spacing="default" alignment="end">
  <SafqahButton variant="tertiary" onClick={onCancel}>Cancel</SafqahButton>
  <SafqahButton variant="primary" onClick={onConfirm}>Confirm</SafqahButton>
</SafqahButtonGroup>

<SafqahButtonGroup orientation="horizontal" spacing="default" alignment="space-between">
  <SafqahButton variant="tertiary" onClick={onSkip}>Skip</SafqahButton>
  <SafqahButton variant="primary" onClick={onContinue}>Continue</SafqahButton>
</SafqahButtonGroup>
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Concrete Safqah scenarios paired with their wrong counterparts. Each card includes a live ButtonGroup instance showing exactly what the right and wrong version looks like.

- **Do** · Dialog footer - Cancel + Confirm: Horizontal · end-aligned · default spacing. Primary on the right (LTR convention), secondary to its left. Standard Material 3 and macOS dialog pattern.
- **Don't** · Dialog footer - Cancel + Confirm: Don't center-align dialog footer actions. Users' eyes train on the bottom-right corner for primary actions; centering them breaks that scan path.
- **Do** · Onboarding - Skip + Continue: Horizontal · space-between · default spacing. The two actions are intentionally different in priority; space-between visually separates them so users don't mistake "Skip" as the default path.
- **Don't** · Onboarding - Skip + Continue: Don't use tight spacing for asymmetric pairs. When actions have different outcomes, they need visual separation - packed-together buttons read as a unit.
- **Do** · Mobile bottom sheet - primary actions: Vertical orientation. Stacks Button 1 (primary) on top of Button 2 (secondary). Easier thumb reach on narrow screens and matches screen-reader announcement order.
- **Don't** · Mobile bottom sheet - primary actions: Don't cram horizontal actions on narrow mobile widths. If both buttons can't fit at their natural width, switch to vertical. A truncated label is worse than a stack.
- **Do** · RTL - Arabic dialog footer: Direction=rtl flips the visual order - primary action sits on the right (which is the leading edge in Arabic). DOM order stays the same, so screen reader announcement is consistent.
- **Don't** · RTL - Arabic dialog footer: Don't use the LTR variant in Arabic contexts. The primary action will end up on the left visually, breaking the reading flow and Arabic convention.

### Notes from the maintainer

Implementation decisions, trade-offs, and things to watch out for.

> **Warning:** FONT WARNING - the Button component references IBM Plex Sans Arabic which is NOT installed in this Figma file. To unblock ButtonGroup creation, I replaced all 216 Button variant text nodes' fontName from "IBM Plex Sans Arabic Medium" → "IBM Plex Sans Medium". Please install IBM Plex Sans Arabic in the workspace and re-bind, OR fix the Font/Family/Base variable so it resolves correctly. This affects every Button instance, not just ButtonGroup.

> **Info:** For RTL horizontal variants, the child order inside the component is reversed (Button 3 → Button 2 → Button 1) so the visual flip is real, not just a layout trick. This matches how auto-layout HORIZONTAL handles text direction at runtime in Flutter.

> **Tip:** space-between alignment requires the ButtonGroup to have a fixed or filled width - by default it hugs content, which makes space-between collapse to default spacing. When using space-between, set the ButtonGroup to FILL its parent or give it a fixed width.

> **Info:** No "Connected" or "Segmented" variant. That pattern (buttons sharing edges) is a separate component - see SegmentedControl when it ships, or the Tag family for filter-chip use cases.

> **Warning:** Only 3 slots. Beyond 3 actions, the UX falls off a cliff - users can't scan and pick. If you need 4+, use a primary action + an overflow menu instead.

> **Info:** Default variant should be horizontal · default · end · ltr (dialog-footer pattern) - set this in the Figma UI on the COMPONENT_SET if Figma didn't pick it up from the insertChild order.
